# `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` order two strings byte by byte, on every target.
#
# The checker has always allowed a string on both sides, and Go, JavaScript and
# Kotlin compare strings natively, as the constant folder does. The interpreter
# read both operands as numbers, every string as 0, so no string came before
# another: a sort by name left the names where they were. The words are state,
# so nothing here is folded before it runs.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

component main ui.node {
    var words = ["pear", "apple", "fig"]

    ui.text(value=words.format(", "))
}

// `words` in order, each put before the first it comes before.
func sorted(words list[string]) list[string] {
    var out list[string] = []
    for var w = words {
        var at = out.length()
        for at > 0 && w < out[at - 1] {
            at -= 1
        }
        out.insert(at, w)
    }
    return out
}

func testStringsAreOrdered(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.words[1] < c.words[0])
    t.assert(!(c.words[0] < c.words[1]))
    t.assert(c.words[0] > c.words[2])
    t.assert(c.words[2] <= c.words[0] && c.words[0] <= c.words[0])
    t.assert(c.words[0] >= c.words[0] && !(c.words[1] >= c.words[2]))
    t.assert(c.words[0] < "pears")
    t.assert(sorted(c.words).format(", ") == "apple, fig, pear")
}
